newsitem.title: USA: Trial of Orange County asst treasurer postponed.
newsitem.headline: Trial of Orange County asst treasurer postponed.

text.p: The trial of former Orange County, Calif., Assistant Treasurer Matthew Raabe has been postponed until March 5, court officials said.
The trial was expected to begin on January 21, but was rescheduled to give defense attorneys more time to prepare their case, the officials said.
"It doesn't change anything for us. We're ready to do the trial and we'll be ready on March 5," Deputy Orange County District Attorney Matthew Anderson said.
Raabe was indicted in May 1995 on six felony counts, including counts of making untrue material statements in the sale of securities and misappropriation of public funds.
Former county Treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to the same charges and was sentenced last month to a year in county jail and fined $100,000.

Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the Federal Bankruptcy Code on December 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. It was the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in June.
